# Third-party code

## libvterm 0.3.3 (`deps/libvterm`, MIT, see its `LICENSE`)

The terminal state machine behind the `vterm` screen engine. Upstream lives in
Bazaar on Launchpad; this tree comes from the git mirror Neovim kept of it.

| What | Value |
|---|---|
| Added with | `git read-tree --prefix=deps/libvterm -u v0.3.3^{tree}` after fetching the tag: one plain commit, no merge, so history stays linear; its `git-subtree-dir:` / `git-subtree-split:` trailers are what `git subtree` reads |
| Upstream commit | `9d6d2112335080312ef8c36667fa717ded4f7daf` (tag `v0.3.3`) |
| Release tarball | `libvterm-0.3.3.tar.gz`, sha256 `09156f43dd2128bd347cbeebe50d9a571d32c64e0cf18d211197946aff7226e0`, the same file as Debian's `libvterm_0.3.3.orig.tar.gz` |
| Checked | `src/` and `include/` equal the tarball's, file for file |

Changes on top of upstream, each its own commit (`git log -- deps/libvterm`):

1. `src/encoding/DECdrawing.inc` and `uk.inc`: generated by upstream's Makefile from the
   `.tbl` files with Perl; copied from the release tarball, which ships them, so a build
   needs only a C compiler.

Nothing else in libvterm is changed; py-screen's own C code reaches libvterm through its
headers only.

To update, keep it flat the same way: fetch the new tag, `git rm -rq deps/libvterm`,
`git read-tree --prefix=deps/libvterm -u <tag>^{tree}`, commit with the two trailers
naming the new upstream commit, then redo change 1 from that release's tarball and
check its sha256 against Debian's `.dsc`. (`git subtree pull --squash` also works from
the trailers, tested 0.3.2 → 0.3.3, but it adds a merge commit.)
